priceScope: Conditional whole-recipient annual-cost reference for a narrow Evanston service channel; not a verified marginal gift offer

what: Metropolitan Tenants Organization helps renters understand their rights and resolve housing problems.
Its hotline, tenant organizing and advocacy support safer housing and more stable tenancies.
In Evanston, MTO also provides advice, referrals and training under a public-service contract.
strengths: Free advice and organizing can address housing problems before they escalate.
Original city records identify current services and distinguish MTO from its legal-service partner.
Housing stability offers plausible health and household-resource benefits.
reservations: Reported issues are not unique tenants or measured successful housing outcomes.
Clinical utility, net resource gains and additional funding response remain judgment inputs.
The reference charges all recipient expense to one narrow channel and is not an organization-wide efficiency ranking.

sections.what: MTO is the Chicago-based charitable recipient, EIN 36-3351193. It provides tenant-rights advice, organizing, advocacy and referrals; legal representation is not automatically MTO-only output. The current official About page describes these services and links the donation route; no transaction was made. [Program](https://www.tenants-rights.org/about/)
sections.monitoring: The newer City renewal memorandum reports 365 MTO issues between January 1 and October 1,2025, plus approximately 21 text cases with unknown overlap. These are not 365 unique households, successful tenancies or annual completions. The FY 2025 CAPER reports approximately 464 calls jointly handled by MTO and LCBH; those cannot be added as MTO-only outcomes. The return describes a generic 8,000–10,000 annual hotline range, not a deduplicated FY 2025 success cohort. These current records establish activity, not causal clinical utility or net earnings.
sections.qualitative: The reference retains the initial health mechanism but updates the dated cost and narrow activity proxy. All issue-to-tenant, unique-household, response and utility conversions remain transparent judgments. Advice may avert housing stress, avoid moving costs or help recover deposits, but the same household cash flow is modeled jointly; overlapping positives are discounted and negative burdens are retained. No gross wages, legal claims, deposits and landlord losses are counted as independent free gains. Broader organizing, policy and job-access effects remain unquantified, not demonstrated zero. The model is a conditional limited-channel reference, not a calibrated probability-weighted expected value.
sections.cost:
Original FY 2025 Form 990 reports$980,346 recipient annual expenses, including administration and fundraising. ScheduleD reconciles the same recognized cost; blank addbacks do not prove absence of volunteer, partner or full economic costs. Charging all annual expense to a January–October narrow Evanston channel deliberately leaves broader recipient benefits unpriced and partly mismatches periods. We do not annualize the 365 issues or use the$91,600 joint public-contract ceiling as whole-recipient cost. The reference uses judged unique tenant households and incremental service response, with a finite stress-health improvement and one-off net household savings. Clinical and signed income components are shown separately below; equivalent income welfare years are not measured QALYs. Initial$21.815 M is retained as a diagnostic, not the current price. Updated cost/activity and explicit household burdens—not stronger causal evidence—explain the change.

The conditional reference is about $18.2 million per better life: 0.417 clinical QALYs plus 0.120 signed household-resource equivalents. The proxy is roughly $2,686 of whole-recipient annual expense per documented issue—not a marginal price for one successful tenant case. Judged household resource successes receive $600 net one-off resources; other exposed households lose $50 in process costs. The latter are retained even when there is no clinical or resource success.
sections.funding: FY 2025 original revenue$944,614 and ending net assets$601,222 do not establish liquid reserves or a next-donation gap. The City 2026 renewal request has a$91,600 not-to-exceed joint ceiling; the$46,800 base is split$36,800 MTO/$10,000 LCBH. Additional services are billed as incurred; prior under-spending means a ceiling is not a realized capacity expansion. Unrestricted-donor response is judged, and zero additionality is tested. Updated public funding and broader services matter to the counterfactual; no priced marginal commitment was verified.
